prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the nearby garage contents from the farther driveway, lawn, and pickup: the tractor, carts, shelving, and doorway edges are roughly 0.5–3 m away, while the truck is about 5–10 m away and the lawn is farther. Across frames 1–3, the camera turns right, shifting the tractor and shelving left or out of view while the driveway occupies more of the view; the pickup remains ahead-right and does not show a clear approach or retreat. In frame 4, a person appears ahead-right at roughly 1–2 m, then in frame 5 becomes very near—probably within arm's reach—and is partly cut off by the right edge. Bright silhouettes and continuous surfaces make near/far ordering clearer than in the overexposed RGB, but the map gives no dependable metric scale and appears unreliable around object boundaries, the bright floor, the open doorway, and the person's blurred outline.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates several spatial regions, including vehicles on the left inside the garage, the pickup ahead-right outside, and a person entering on the right in frames 4–5; it also makes partial occlusion and objects crossing frame boundaries easier to see than in RGB. The indoor vehicle occupies much of the left foreground in frames 1–2, a small object identified as a chair lies nearer the center, and the pickup stays higher and farther ahead as the view rotates right through frames 2–4. The person is ahead-right in frame 4 and much larger and partly out of view at the right edge in frame 5, indicating decreasing separation from roughly 1–2 m to within about 1 m; no reliable facing direction or gaze can be recovered from the masks. Many class labels are clearly unreliable in context—such as “motorcycle” on the tractor, “surfboard” on the driveway or foreground structure, and “airplane/bird” on small regions—and the large frame-5 masks merge or misclassify surrounding surfaces, so distances and object-to-object spacing are only approximate.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only one body, in frame 4, located ahead-right at roughly 1–2 m; its joints place the head above the torso and the arms raised or bent near shoulder/head height. The skeleton's asymmetry suggests the body is turned obliquely rather than squarely toward the camera, but the sparse joints do not establish gaze direction, and no separate hand skeleton is visible. The body is absent from frames 1–3, then the much closer, partly out-of-frame person in frame 5 receives no skeleton even though the RGB and other maps show that person near the camera wearer's right side and likely within arm's reach. Pose therefore exposes approximate limb configuration that is hard to resolve in the blurred RGB, but it is unreliable for temporal tracking, facing direction, hands, occluded joints, and the closest frame.
